## Runs 6–7 — inherited SdH spot checks, raw → onset → spectral stability

Only this session's TSVs are used. These completed runs were missing from the analysis record at handoff. Channel sr1 probes B_1−B_2; signed voltage is normalized by measured drain current (sr0 gain −10⁶), with commanded-current normalization differing by at most about 2%. Both runs stayed below 12% of the 5 kΩ full scale; gate currents stayed below 216 pA and sample T below 1.30 K. Negative Rxx excursions are retained, not rectified or logarithmically clipped; field asymmetrization is unavailable from these positive-field records.

Run 6 (electron, n=+3.2×10¹²) contains a near-harmonic comb and its carrying low-frequency onset is censored; the coarse B<1 T leg cannot Nyquist its 33.1 T Luttinger frequency. Run 7 (hole, n=−1.2×10¹²) provides the cleaner low-field anchor: helper onset 0.71388 T, with candidate ~4.7/6.6 T components and a ~12.3 T feature near F_L=12.41 T. The candidate pair sums to ~11.3 T, roughly 0.91 of nominal F_L, but the singleton and pair must share one fitted scale before any assignment. Harmonic flags are diagnostics, not permission to discard a Luttinger partner.

**Verdict: B_1−B_2 remains uninformative for a unique stacking assignment.** The hole fan is a limited next test of density dispersion and sampling-grid reproduction. The ABAB model at n=−1.2 predicts 5.863/6.545 T, separated by only 0.682 T: unresolved in a 0.714–6 T record (δF=0.810 T), and more so using the higher onset of the second observed component. No absent-partner claim is permitted. Model overlays (ABAB and trilayer), one global density scale, and F_L-tone origin checks remain outstanding. The two zero-field ridges in run 5 also leave a spatial-doping confound; a single voltage pair cannot localize their contributions.

## HERA — hole-side density-dispersion fan for the stacking investigation

Gates A/B/C are satisfied by measure cells 2–34, SAFETIES cell 18 (execution 10), and runs 0–3; handoff cells 44/46 restore state0 and confirm the same bound kernel. The existing E1 grant remains engaged per the operator's brief. Recipe: `landau-fan-vti`, governed by `tetralayer-stacking-fs-count` Step 4. Runs 6/7 are now analyzed in ana: choose the hole side because its low-field oscillations have an uncensored helper onset (run 7, 0.7138767 T), whereas run 6 has a censored near-residual/harmonic comb. This fan tests density dispersion and uniform-1/B reproduction of the observed spectral set on B_1−B_2; it is **not promised to resolve all pockets or deliver a unique stacking call**.

**One floored design:** 66 B rows, uniform in 1/B from the measured onset to 6 T; 9 paired-gate density points −1.20…−0.95×10¹² cm⁻² at D=0, Si=0, base T, 10 nA drive, fixed sr1 sensitivity 50 µV (5 kΩ), 3 s fast-point dwell (10τ at 0.3 s/24 dB). Run-5 calibration gives TG −0.27703…−0.20541 V and BG −0.46504…−0.37235 V, well within committed validators. Ratio is data-calibrated; absolute density remains geometry-prior and D=0 comes from the CNP-resistance symmetry minimum, not an independently calibrated electric field.

**Sampling and resolution:** F_L(max)=12.407 T; Δ(1/B)=0.0189867 T⁻¹ clears Nyquist both for F_L and the observed 26.2 T harmonic (Nyquist frequency 26.334 T). It is finer than run 7's local spacing 0.02/B_onset²≈0.0392 T⁻¹. Density step 0.03125×10¹² is below half the lowest-field g=4 ray spacing, 0.03452×10¹². Usable nominal record length 1.23414 T⁻¹ gives δF=0.8103 T. The forward model (`fs_count_b0.abab_fs`, SI input n×10¹⁶ m⁻²) predicts branches 4.069/5.751 T at −0.95 and 5.863/6.545 T at −1.20. The smallest predicted orbit spans 5.02 nominal periods; reducing B_max below about 5.82 T loses that target. **Per-tone caveat:** the observed ~4.7 T component starts only near 1.03 T, so its effective record is shorter; five periods and pair resolution are not established for both real tones. ABAB pair separation is below 2δF across nearly all this window; only the low-|n| edge marginally clears the nominal split criterion. This is the gate-accessible low-density exception regime, not the preferred |n|≥2–3×10¹² hole regime (unreachable within the existing limits). Unresolved partners remain “not resolvable,” never “searched and absent.” The meaningful test is branch motion versus F_L and harmonic motion; a decisive two-pocket classification may remain unavailable.

**Coverage trade:** electron densities, CNP, the final −1.20…−1.27 gate-edge interval, and B>6 T are excluded. The electron side needs a separate onset-quality check; the narrow gate-edge extension worsens branch separation. Repeating this same grid to 10 T would add about 29 minutes of bare ramp plus roughly 2 minutes of rows while improving δF only to 0.769 T, still unable to separate the anchor pair. A full two-sided fan would mix different sampling/onset requirements and spend rows near an uninformative CNP.

**Price:** run 5 at NPLC=1 measured median 1.098 s/point with a 1 s dwell. Budget 3.2 s/point here for 3 s dwell, paired gate sets, and the added file thermometer: 594 points →31.68 min; 66×4 s for magnet settle/slow delay/flyback →4.4 min; 0→6 T at 0.137 T/min →43.80 min; 2 min setup plus 10% margin →90 min. No return traverse: leave field at 6 T and gates at the final line point for the next decision. The shared n=−1.20 column is the acquisition-quality comparison against run 7.

**Checkpoints:** inspect the first three landed rows for leakage, clipped/flat lock-in values, drain current and temperature; then every ~15–20 min and at B≈2 T compare the anchor column's developing oscillations with run 7. Initial rows are near onset and absence there alone is not a wash-out. Per-point guards stop on the existing 1 nA gate-current trip, rail approach, loss of drain current, or departure from base T; both file thermometer freshness checks run before acquisition and periodically. Global dynamic range uses the run-7 maximum 587 Ω, increased by the 1.20/0.95 lower-density factor to ~742 Ω; 5 kΩ FS gives >6× that conservative anchor, with a rail guard for unforeseen MR. Every followed channel has a live plot.

Preconditions print expected/actual thermometry, heater ranges, Si state, lock-in settings, routing, magnet PS/output and validators before any write. **VTI magnet caution:** kernel interruption does not stop a ramp already commanded to the supply (rig card overrides generic abort wording); the current row's target can still be reached. After any stop, read actual field and gates before deciding another move. No limits, ramp pacing, Si voltage, or heater settings are changed.

# Preconditions: all reads before any write. Same-kernel SAFETIES cell 18 is committed.
def _fan_expect(label, actual, expected, ok):
    print(f'{label}: expected {expected}; actual {actual}')
    assert ok, f'fan precondition failed: {label}'
for _p,_lim in ((k_tg.volt,(-.3,1.)),(k_bg.volt,(-1.3,2.)),

                (magnet.field,(-10.,10.)),(heater.sample_setpoint,(0.,100.)),

    _fan_expect(_p.full_name+' validator',_got,_lim,_got==_lim)
_fan_expect('session caps',(B_SESSION_CAP,T_SESSION_CAP),(10,100),B_SESSION_CAP==10 and T_SESSION_CAP==100)
for _name in ('T_sample','T_vaporizer'):
    assert_thermometry_live(_name,VTI.temp_logfile_candidates[_name],max_age=15,max_period=12)

def _fan_guard(station,data):
